'''David Frank Bocian''' (born 1950)<ref>{{Citation|title=Faculties, Publications, and Doctoral Theses in Chemistry and Chemical Engineering at United States Universities|page=125|author=American Chemical Society. Committee on Professional Training|date=1991}}</ref> is an American [[chemist]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/89632889/|title=CMU chemist designs tiny molecular wire|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|location=[[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]]|date=October 19, 1994|access-date=May 17, 2026|page=12|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Closed access}}</ref> He was a [[distinguished professor]] in the department of [[chemistry]] at the [[University of California, Riverside]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://profiles.ucr.edu/app/home/profile/dbocian|title=David F Bocian|work=[[University of California, Riverside]]|access-date=May 16, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chem.ucr.edu/faculty/physical-chemistry|title=Faculty: Physical Chemistry|work=[[University of California, Riverside]]|access-date=May 16, 2026}}</ref>

In 2000, Bocian was named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic?field_last_name_value=All&field_address_city=All&field_address_when_elected_administrative_area=All&field_address_when_elected_country_code=All&field_year_elected=&field_primary_aaas_section=All&field_status_value=All&field_year_status_changed_value=&name_combine=bocian&field_institutional_affiliation_value=|title=Historic Fellows|work=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|access-date=June 5, 2026}}</ref>
